root_cause: Use of truncating integer division (>> 3, i.e. floor(x/8)) to compute the number of 8x8 blocks per dimension, instead of ceiling division, when the corresponding pixel dimension is not guaranteed to be a multiple of 8. The decode loop that walks over blocks uses ceiling-like iteration (steps of 8 covering the full xsize/ysize including a partial last block), creating an inconsistency between the computed grid size (dc_w * dc_h) and the actual number of blocks processed.
findings: In dwa_uncompress(), dc_w and dc_h (the number of 8x8 DC-coefficient blocks per row/column) are computed as td->xsize >> 3 and td->ysize >> 3. This integer division truncates (floors) instead of rounding up.
